**When/where:** 2026-10-14 09:00-12:30, Acme HQ, Room 4B · **Runs:** 3 hours 30 minutes
**Attendees:** Dana Ortiz (VP Claims), Priya Nair (Claims Ops Lead), Tom Becker (Head of IT), Lena Fischer (Compliance)
**Facilitator:** Sam Kruger (Pod Lead) · **Pre-reading:** this page only

## What we read

14 documents provided by your team (full registry in Appendix C). The
load-bearing ones: DOC-001 (claims modernization RFP), DOC-003 (current-state process map), DOC-007 (SLA agreement with the adjuster network), DOC-011 (data retention policy)

## What the documents say

<!-- 3-6 factual claims that frame the working session. Claims, not conclusions. -->

- The average claim takes 19 days from first notice to first payment (DOC-003)
- First-notice intake runs through three separate systems with manual re-keying (DOC-003)
- The adjuster network is contracted to respond within 48 hours of assignment (DOC-007)
- Claim records must be retained for seven years after closure (DOC-011)

## Where the documents disagree

<!-- The top contradictions by severity — usually 3-5. Each ends in its resolving question.
     Full detail in Appendix B. -->

1. DOC-001 says the portal replaces all intake channels; DOC-003 says phone intake stays for large commercial losses. **Which channels must the portal retire in the first release?** (CON-01)
2. DOC-007 says adjusters respond within 48 hours; DOC-001 targets same-day assignment. **Which time commitment governs the first release?** (CON-02)

## What nobody has written down

<!-- 8-12 questions max on the page, grouped by agenda block. Full list in Appendix A.
     Only questions routed "workshop" — pre-workshop questions were already emailed. -->

- **Problem:** Which claim types hurt the most today, and what does a delayed claim cost the business per day? (Q-01)
- **Success metric:** Which single number will tell us the portal worked, and which system will it be read from? (Q-04)
- **Constraints:** Is the legacy policy database frozen for the duration of the project? (Q-07)

## Decisions we need from the room

<!-- The must-leave-with list, 3-5 items. If the workshop produces only these, it succeeded. -->

1. The one success metric — and the named system it will be read from
2. The product-owner commitment: a named PO at the agreed hours, or proxy mode
3. Whether phone intake for large commercial losses is in or out of the first release

## Agenda

| Block | Time | Output |
|-------|------|--------|
| The problem, in your words | 45 min | Problem narrative, current state, who hurts and how much |
| The three outcomes | 45 min | Business, software, capability — one sentence each |
| The one metric | 30 min | The metric, its baseline (or the admission nobody knows it), its source system |
| Constraints | 30 min | What's fixed, what's negotiable |
| Product ownership | 20 min | Named PO with hours, or proxy mode acknowledged |
| Tooling status | 10 min | Procurement status, who unblocks it, fallback date |
